# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## Primary Classification by Core Mechanic

---

### 1. LOOP-DRAWING GAMES
*Objective: Draw a single continuous closed loop through the grid*

#### 1.1 Unconstrained Path Loop
- **Slitherlink** — Loop drawn between dots; numbers indicate how many sides of a cell are used
- **Masyu** — Loop must satisfy circle constraints (straight through white, turn at black)

#### 1.2 Cell-Traversal Loop
*Loop passes through cell centers*

##### 1.2.1 With Regional/Area Constraints
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop passes through rooms once; must alternate between moon-only and sun-only rooms
- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop must either turn at ALL or go STRAIGHT through ALL white circles within each bold-line area

##### 1.2.2 With Directional Constraints
- **Nagareru** — Wind direction cells restrict which way loop can travel; arrows dictate loop direction
- **Suraromu** — Loop starts/ends at numbered circle; must pass through all "Gates" in numbered order

##### 1.2.3 With Point/Marker Constraints
- **Mid-loop** — Black circles must be the midpoint of straight segments passing through them
- **Yajilin** — Arrow-number clues indicate black cell counts in a direction; loop avoids black cells

---

### 2. REGION-DIVISION GAMES
*Objective: Partition the grid into defined regions or blocks*

#### 2.1 Divide into Rectangles/Squares
- **Shikaku** — Divide grid into rectangles; each contains exactly one number equal to its area

#### 2.2 Divide into Polyomino Shapes
- **LITS** — Each bold-line area contributes one tetromino; all colored cells connect; no 2×2 fill
- **Five Cells** — Divide into pentominoes; numbers indicate how many block-boundary lines surround a cell
- **Fillomino** — Fill grid with numbered blocks; each block's size equals its number; same-size blocks don't touch

#### 2.3 Divide into Specific Shapes
- **Sashigane** — Divide into L-shaped blocks; circles mark the bend; arrows point toward the bend

#### 2.4 Divide into Paired Color Blocks
- **Double Choco** — Each block contains matching white and gray regions of identical shape
- **Nuritwin** — Each outlined region contains exactly two same-sized shaded blocks

---

### 3. CELL-SHADING / PAINTING GAMES
*Objective: Determine which cells to color black (or shade)*

#### 3.1 Connectivity and Shape Rules
- **Nurikabe** — White "islands" of given size separated by connected black "river"; no 2×2 black
- **Heyawake** — Black cells don't touch; white cells stay connected; white runs can't cross more than two rooms
- **Hitori** — Shade cells so no number repeats in any row/column; black cells don't touch; white cells connected

#### 3.2 Count-Based Adjacency Rules
- **Kurodoko** — Numbers count total white cells visible from that cell horizontally and vertically
- **Kurotto** — Numbers in circles equal sum of connected black cell groups extending from them
- **Usowan** — Numbers show adjacent black cell count, but exactly one number per bold-line room is wrong

#### 3.3 Shape-Constrained Shading
- **Choco Banana** — Black regions must be rectangles/squares; white regions must NOT be rectangles/squares
- **Shakashaka** — Place half-cell triangles so remaining white areas form only rectangles/squares
- **Norinori** — Shade cells in dominoes; each bold-line area contains exactly two shaded cells

#### 3.4 Shading with Gravity/Physical Rules
- **Sto-stone** — Shade cells in rooms per number clue; when "dropped" downward, stones fill bottom half exactly

#### 3.5 Shading to Create a Maze
- **Nurimeizu** — Shade whole rooms to create walls; shortest path S→G passes all circles, avoids triangles

#### 3.6 Shading to Reveal an Image
- **Tilepaint** — Color entire tiles based on diagonal-cell row/column counts; solution reveals an object outline

---

### 4. NUMBER-PLACEMENT GAMES
*Objective: Fill cells with numbers satisfying given constraints*

#### 4.1 Latin Square / Uniqueness Constraint
- **Sudoku** — Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 box exactly once

#### 4.2 Room-Based Number Sets
- **Ripple Effect** — Each bold-line room contains 1 through N (room size); duplicates in a row/column must be separated by at least that number's value
- **Makaro** — Each room contains 1 through N; arrow cells indicate which neighbor holds the maximum value; same numbers in adjacent rooms can't touch

#### 4.3 Block-Size Encoding
- **Fillomino** *(also in Region-Division)* — Numbers encode the size of the block they belong to

#### 4.4 Crossword-Style Number Fill
- **Nansuke** — Fill white cells with numbers from a given list; numbers read left-to-right or top-to-bottom

---

### 5. PATH / MOVEMENT GAMES
*Objective: Trace or move elements along paths through the grid*

#### 5.1 Connect Matching Elements
- **Numberlink** — Connect same-number pairs with non-crossing, non-branching lines filling all cells
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect numbered islands with bridges (≤2 per pair); all islands linked

#### 5.2 Move Elements to Target Areas
- **Satogaeri** — Move circles horizontally/vertically into their country (region); paths cannot cross
- **Yosenabe** — Move numbered circles straight into gray areas; gray area number equals sum of entering circles

#### 5.3 Sequential Path Placement
- **Hebi** — Place snake segments numbered 1–5 (head to tail) in white cells; snakes can't touch; directional attack rules apply

---

### 6. SYMBOL/MARK PLACEMENT GAMES
*Objective: Place specific symbols in cells according to rules*

#### 6.1 Light/Visibility Placement
- **Akari** — Place light bulbs in white cells; numbered cells constrain adjacent bulbs; every white cell must be lit; bulbs can't see each other

#### 6.2 Line/Stroke Fill
- **Juosan** — Fill every cell with — or |; territory numbers constrain the difference in counts; — can't stack more than 2 rows high; | can't span more than 2 columns wide

#### 6.3 Triangle Placement
- **Shakashaka** *(also in Cell-Shading)* — Place half-cell triangles so white remainders are only rectangles

---

### 7. BLOCK / CHAIN STRUCTURE GAMES
*Objective: Identify or construct connected block structures with meta-constraints*

#### 7.1 Chain Uniqueness
- **Chained Block** — Black cell groups form blocks; blocks touching diagonally form chains; no chain may contain two blocks of the same size/shape

#### 7.2 Evolving Block Sequences
- **Evolomino** — Draw squares along arrow routes; each successive block along an arrow adds exactly one square to the previous shape without rotation/flip

---

### 8. PROMONTORY / CONNECTIVITY GAMES
*Objective: Ensure white cell networks satisfy endpoint and linearity rules*

- **Nurimisaki** — Circle cells are "promontories" (exactly one white neighbor); numbers indicate straight white-cell run length; all white cells connected; no 2×2 white or black

---

### 9. COMPOSITE / HYBRID GAMES
*Games that combine two or more distinct mechanic categories*

| Game | Primary Mechanic | Secondary Mechanic |
|---|---|---|
| **Yajilin** | Loop-drawing | Cell-shading (black cells placed by clues) |
| **Suraromu** | Loop-drawing | Ordered gate traversal (sequence constraint) |
| **Dotchi-Loop** | Loop-drawing | Regional all-or-nothing constraint |
| **Pencils** | Path-drawing from tips | Block-size encoding along pencil bodies |
| **Norinori** | Cell-shading (dominoes) | Regional containment (2 per area) |
| **Nuritwin** | Cell-shading | Region-division (paired blocks) |

---

## Cross-Cutting Constraint Types

| Constraint Type | Games Exhibiting It |
|---|---|
| **Adjacency counts** | Akari, Kurotto, Usowan, Shakashaka |
| **No 2×2 of same color** | Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu, Norinori, Nuritwin |
| **All same-type cells connected** | Nurikabe, Hitori, Heyawake, Usowan, LITS, Nuritwin |
| **Regional containment (exactly N per area)** | Norinori, Nuritwin, Double Choco, Heyawake |
| **Single loop** | Masyu, Slitherlink, Dotchi-Loop, Moon-or-Sun, Nagareru, Mid-loop, Suraromu, Yajilin |
| **No same-value neighbors** | Sudoku, Fillomino, Makaro, Ripple Effect |
| **Directional/visibility rays** | Akari, Kurodoko, Yajilin, Hebi |
| **Gravity/drop mechanic** | Sto-stone |
